question: What is dispersion? Distinguish between absolute and relative measures of dispersion, and explain why the standard deviation is considered the best measure.

points.label: Meaning
points.description: Dispersion is the degree to which observations are scattered around a central value; an average alone does not show this spread.

points.label: Absolute measures
points.description: Absolute measures are expressed in the same units as the data: range, quartile deviation, mean deviation and standard deviation.

points.label: Relative measures
points.description: Relative measures are ratios free of units, such as coefficient of range, coefficient of quartile deviation, coefficient of mean deviation and coefficient of variation; they are used to compare series with different units or averages.

points.label: Standard deviation
points.description: Standard deviation is the positive square root of the mean of squared deviations from the arithmetic mean.

points.label: Why it is the best
points.description: It is rigidly defined, based on all observations, suitable for further algebraic treatment and less affected by sampling fluctuations; it is independent of change of origin but not of scale. Its limitation is that it gives more weight to extreme values.
points.basis: Statistics: properties, merits and limitations of standard deviation
